evidence: Optical diagnostics on exploratory, unvalidated inherited snow populations, with representation-dependent particle arithmetic and uncapped extreme tails. Snow-only geometric-optics extinction retains explicit number/area moments; height-resolved illumination read from an existing molecular-sky solution; thin-path HG radiance and independent all-order slab flux sensitivities. No lunar observation or resolved storm image.
reading_rule: Use a run and level together. Number_m3 is bin integrated; area is its number-weighted particle mean. Q_ext=2 is wavelength independent. The 5% beam distance is a snow-only optical range, not a prediction of human visibility under twilight or Earthlight. Extinction is evaluated from the time-mean population as a homogeneous medium: exp(-mean optical depth) is not the time mean of transmission through intermittent snow. Thin directional outputs apply at tau=.05 in exposed snow with approximately clear incident illumination and isotropized diffuse light; a short sightline deep inside an opaque cloud does not meet that condition. slab fluxes use a distinct infinite-slab geometry and cannot be substituted for those radiances or used alone to infer image detail or a visible horizon.

assumptions.size_parameter_regime: dimensions and monomers much larger than visible wavelengths
assumptions.particle_area: population settling area used for every ray direction; no spherical envelope substituted or optical orientation distribution solved

population_numerical_audit.evidence: Numerical audit of inherited exploratory, unvalidated column populations. Arithmetic counterexamples establish nonhomogeneity in represented area; paired short-column runs quantify sensitivity for one seed and one shallow prescribed cloud. The unchanged full heavy replay, when included, traces collision arithmetic and extreme-tail timing without revising the physical model.
population_numerical_audit.reading_rule: All extensive particle numbers, mass ledgers and observers are normalized to one square metre. Cloud moments are equally spaced post-fill samples averaged over the whole prescribed depth. Freezing-level fluxes use individual settling speeds to infer concentration. Number, mass and area are retained separately; open size bins are bookkeeping, not physically admitted particle dimensions. Paired-seed differences after representation-dependent branching include later Monte Carlo divergence and are not an ensemble estimate of systematic bias.

lighting.reading_rule: Bilinear interpolation in physical radius and geometric solar elevation of the saved spectral moments. Moment 0 is integral L dOmega; moments 5 and 6 are downward/upward horizontal flux. Direct light uses independent analytic shell intersections and a finite uniform Sun. XYZ weights already contain the shielded TSIS-1 source and 360–830 nm photopic response.
limits: Molecular clear sky at a 294.9 K surface; snow population column uses the 301 K resort interpolation.
Snow and supercooled cloud do not feed back on this incident clear-sky field.

Earth proxy uses the admitted 7.8 lux full-Earth normalization with shielded-solar colour; Earth spectral shape, phase, rotating continents and its larger finite disk are not modeled; the proxy is a separate source contribution, not a combined sky at a dated orbital configuration.

Aggregate morphology, orientation, transparency and breakup remain population/optical assumptions. The inherited uncapped aggregation law can generate nonphysical extreme tails without an upper size bound. Their area remains in the total and is exposed separately in 1–10 m and >=10 m size contributions; optical totals with substantial such contributions are runaway-model diagnostics, not credible storm predictions. Sub-metre component values still inherit the population arithmetic and sampling limitations.
HG has no ice-halo peaks or specular facets; neither halo nor sparkle appearance is predicted.

The large-particle extinction paradox includes narrow forward diffraction. Instrument aperture and finite visual targets may recover some scattered light; no human observer model is included. The Q_ext=1 sensitivity counts geometric interception only; it is not a confidence bound or a substitute for a phase matrix plus a specified receiver acceptance angle.
Small supercooled cloud droplets can dominate visibility; water content is not supplied by the snow population.
Conservative grey snow neglects weak visible ice absorption and impurities; no snow-induced spectral colour shift is solved.
No joint three-dimensional snow/cloud/molecular transport or calibrated crystal phase matrix.
